1933, November
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 5.
Page 157 Cont.
Nov. 2 All Souls Day. Remarkable - Sept. 21st. p.m. John Coneff phoned "Enroll W. C. Hickey ... very low, in Ser. Mass As'n." Same W.C.H. died at 6:30 p.m. same day ..... Hickey had been very generous in helpin poor failing to pay his insurance .... wife had thrown policy away ..... no hope of recovering anything .... .. Sept. 22 Coneff enrolls new organization .... CATHOLIC Beneficial Society ....... Be- yond all hopes Mrs. hickey % this said society recovered and re- ceived what was coming to her ..... $752.59 - insisting on remuner- ating Coneff 10%. She proposed giving 50% which was positively refused. Mrs. Hickey becomes first charter member. Said J. Con- eff opened Office yesterday All Saints Day at 1006 Lafayette Bldg. P.S. Funeral expenses paid by (said) Insurance Co. - % said So- ciety J.C.L. Nov. 4 "Ad" Nov. 2nd brings 500 letters - Nov. 3rd! !!
Page 158
Nov. 2 Mrs. Marie Walsh - 27 - unnaturally thrown into hospital by ungrate- ful husband as insane ....???? released
Grace McCartin - 26 - T.B.5 yrs next January - prayed for many times . ??? again down -but.
Mrs. Grace Hetler - 26 - Hamberg, Pa. T.B. - Methodists --
Nov. 3 Mrs. Helen Grimmer - 35 - last October 18 given two hours to live in hospital. Anointed at that time recovers double operation. Very low again when on July 14 enrolled .. at once improves; now comes with sister, has "yellow jandis" - choice between operation and pro- bably bleed to death or live on as at present - likely not a year .... bitterly biased mother-in-law enrolled today.
3 Dorothy Jozwik - 18 - Kiefer Hosp. T.B. "Hopeless" ....
4 3:30 a.m. enrolled "dying ... Catherine Garrison" by phone from Pon- tiac, enrolled in Ser. Mass As'n
John Ed. Jaglowicz - 8 - tubercular maningitis. Enrolled at 6:15 scientifically hopeless.
Page 159 Nov. Anthony Nowcki - 41 - drinks, curses wife and 4 children .... twice a year to confession ....
Miss Julia Lyons - 53 - had operation for cataract on one eye now almost blind ...
7 Mr. & Mrs. Walsh .... Victim of deplored injustice.
